lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about family.
Sam, you came to my home on Sunday. Come in!
Thank you! This is my first time in your family home.
Sit down, please. This is my mother. This is my father. They are my parents.
Hello! Nice to meet you. And who is this?
This is my sister. And my brother. They live with my parents.
Wow. It is a big family, a lot of people. Where is the kitchen?
There. My mother is in the kitchen. She makes dinner.
I live with my friend Tom. He does not make dinner. He makes noise.
[laugh] Get up, please. Stand up. Dinner is ready.
I get up. It smells very good. Your home is beautiful.
Welcome home, Sam! Now eat.
I am very happy. But my chair is too small, very little.
[laugh] That is my grandmother's chair. See you next time!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is family and home. And I have news: Tom is moving in.
Tom, your friend with the breakup?
Yes. He moved in on Saturday. He brought eleven boxes and one very big plant.
A plant?
He said, "Look after her. Her name is Karen." I now have a bedroom, a living room and a Karen.
[laugh] And how is the housework?
Terrible. Tom says, "I'll do the dishes." Then he sits down and talks about his ex for two hours.
In my home, we have a rule. Everyone does the housework. Even my uncle, and my cousin Rashad.
Your relatives are lovely. How's your family, by the way?
Everyone is fine. My aunt is married again. My grandparents say hello. And my grandmother asked, "Is Sam married yet?"
What did you say?
I said, "No, but he has a plant." Give my love to Karen!
I will. Come over and get together with us. Make yourself at home!
Thank you. But I'm not sure you have a home. Tom has it.
[laugh] See you next time!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is family — and the question: who do you take after?
I take after my father. He was a baker. He got up at four o'clock every day, and he never complained.
I take after my father too. He's retired, and he teaches salsa. Like father, like son — except I can't dance.
Sam! Your dad brought you up to dance, I'm sure of it.
He tried. Every Sunday, in the living room. We argued about everything: the music, the steps, my feet.
That's what a close relationship looks like. My parents were strict, but they always gave us support.
And you and your sister shared a room for eighteen years. How did you get along?
Most of the time, well. We shared clothes, secrets and a bed lamp. Sometimes we shared a fight.
Blood is thicker than water, as they say. When my sister got engaged, I cried more than she did.
My mum says the apple doesn't fall far from the tree. And I think she's right: I'm as stubborn as my dad.
Our generation is different from our parents'. We raise kids later, and we move out earlier.
But the family dinner is still the most important meal of the week.
A question for our listeners: who in your family are you most similar to?
And Sam, ring your dad. He's waiting for a salsa video. See you next time!

words.phrase: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree
